record.paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
record.original_question: For a closed PL n-manifold M, call a colored graph G representing M minimal when it realizes the n-complexity c_n(M), meaning that the rank invariant beta_n(G) used in the complexity definition equals c_n(M). Study the graph-theoretic properties of such minimal colored graphs and find combinatorial characterizations of them.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(1) An (n+1)-colored graph is a pair (G, γ) where G = (V(G), E(G)) is a finite multigraph (loops are forbidden, multiple edges are allowed) that is regular of degree n+1, together with an edge-coloring γ : E(G) → Δn = {0, 1, …, n} such that any two edges sharing a vertex receive different colors. For each subset S ⊆ Δn, let G_S denote the subgraph of G whose edges are those colored by elements of S, and let g_S denote the number of connected components of G_S.

(2) From an (n+1)-colored graph (G, γ) one constructs an n-dimensional simplicial cell complex K(G) as follows: take an n-simplex σ_v for each vertex v of G, label the vertices of σ_v injectively by Δn, and for every edge of color c joining v and w glue the (n−1)-faces of σ_v and σ_w opposite to the c-labeled vertices via the unique color-preserving simplicial map. The graph G is said to represent the closed PL n-manifold M when |K(G)| is PL-homeomorphic to M.

(3) Define, for an (n+1)-colored graph G representing a closed PL n-manifold, the invariant
   β_n(G) = (#V(G))/2 − 1
(equivalently, half the number of vertices minus 1). The n-complexity (gem-complexity) of a closed PL n-manifold M is
   c_n(M) = min { β_n(G) : G is an (n+1)-colored graph representing M }.
A colored graph G representing M is called minimal if β_n(G) = c_n(M).

Problem. Investigate the graph-theoretic structure of minimal (n+1)-colored graphs representing closed PL n-manifolds, and provide intrinsic combinatorial characterizations of minimality. More precisely, identify necessary and/or sufficient combinatorial conditions on an (n+1)-colored graph (G, γ) — for example, conditions on the numbers g_S of components of its color-induced subgraphs, on its bipartite structure, on the regular genus, or on the existence/absence of certain local configurations (dipoles, ρ-pairs, blobs, etc.) — that ensure G realizes the minimum β_n among all colored graphs representing |K(G)|.
artifact.category_tag: Crystallizations and gem-complexity of PL manifolds
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on crystallizations and gem-complexity (Casali, Cristofori, and collaborators) continues to compute gem-complexity case by case and to catalogue minimal colored graphs in low dimensions (e.g., PL 4-manifolds up to gem-complexity 8, lens spaces, hyperbolic 3-manifolds), but no general combinatorial characterization of minimal colored graphs has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Cataloguing PL 4-manifolds by gem-complexity
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm subdivides PL 4-manifolds via crystallizations; solves PL-homeomorphism problem up to gem-complexity 8.
status_evidence.claim: Research proceeds by enumeration and case studies rather than a general characterization of minimality.

status_evidence.title: Minimal 4-colored graphs representing an infinite family of hyperbolic 3-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs and proves minimality of 4-colored graphs for specific families, indicating no general characterization is available.
status_evidence.claim: Minimality is established case by case, supporting the problem being still open.
